In a challenging environment, with consumption slowing and rising costs, Coca-Cola Andina Bottling Company, controlled equally by the Chadwick Claro, Garcés Silva, Said Handal, and Said Somavía families, reported a profit attributable to owners of 197.164 billion pesos between January and September 2026, an increase of 17.1% compared to the same period the previous year.

The company operates in parts of Argentina, Brazil, and Chile, as well as throughout Paraguay.

In the first nine months, the consolidated sales of the bottling company reached 2.675 trillion pesos, an increase of 11.8% year-over-year, the company reported. The volume reached 691.4 million unit cases (+1.8%), while adjusted consolidated EBITDA grew by 16.9% to 488.932 billion pesos.

YOU MAY BE INTERESTED

Between July and September, the company's profit was 61.482 billion pesos, reflecting a 7.5% growth compared to the same quarter in 2025.

Consolidated net sales for the period rose by 12% to 896.609 billion pesos. According to the company, the increase was driven by higher volumes in Brazil and Chile, a rise in revenue per unit case sold, and the positive effect of currency conversion from operations in Paraguay, Brazil, and Argentina.

Quarterly volume reached 226.1 million unit cases (an increase of 2.5%), and adjusted consolidated EBITDA increased by 12.1% to 149.289 billion pesos.

"These results reflect our ability to continue growing and efficiently manage costs, even in a complex environment characterized by rising oil prices," stated Miguel Ángel Peirano, the executive vice president of Coca-Cola Andina.

The executive attributed the quarterly performance to the developments in operations in Brazil, Chile, and Paraguay, along with strict cost management.

Peirano also highlighted the issuance of a green bond that the company conducted in August in the local market, amounting to 2.5 million UF, at a rate of 2.95% and maturing on September 30, 2030. The issuance achieved a spread of 65 basis points over the reference sovereign.

According to the executive, this is the lowest spread since 2019 for a AA+ corporate issuer, representing "a clear signal of market confidence in our strategy."

Southern Copper Corporation (NYSE:SCCO) is a leading integrated copper producer, primarily engaged in open-pit copper mining, smelting, and refining operations across Peru and Mexico. The company operates major mines, including the Toquepala and Cuajone mines, and is advancing projects like the Tia Maria copper project to enhance copper production capacity. Southern Copper's robust ecosystem includes copper concentrate, refined copper, and copper cathode production, supplemented by molybdenum, silver, and sulfuric acid as byproducts. Leveraging extensive copper reserves and efficient mining infrastructure, the company maintains sustainable operations and competitive advantages in the copper expansion projects of Peru and Mexico.

SECTION 2 COMPANY DESCRIPTION

2.1 Activities

Southern Copper Corporation, a New York Stock Exchange-listed company, is a leading global producer of copper and other metals, with operations centered in Mexico and Peru. Its core business activities encompass the exploration, mining, smelting, and refining of copper, alongside by-products such as molybdenum, zinc, silver, and gold, which are supplied to industries including construction, electronics, and renewable energy. The company's fastest-growing segments include copper production, fueled by rising demand from electric vehicles and infrastructure development, as well as molybdenum extraction for high-strength alloys in manufacturing. By focusing on operational efficiency and strategic investments in new projects, Southern Copper maintains a competitive edge in the global mining sector, emphasizing sustainable practices to support long-term growth. It is the largest Non ferrous metals sector company by market capitalization among NYSE- and TXSE-listed stocks.

Southern Copper Corporation (NYSE:SCCO) is a leading integrated copper producer, primarily engaged in open-pit copper mining, smelting, and refining operations across Peru and Mexico. The company operates major mines, including the Toquepala and Cuajone mines, and is advancing projects like the Tia Maria copper project to enhance copper production capacity. Southern Copper's robust ecosystem includes copper concentrate, refined copper, and copper cathode production, supplemented by molybdenum, silver, and sulfuric acid as byproducts. Leveraging extensive copper reserves and efficient mining infrastructure, the company maintains sustainable operations and competitive advantages in the copper expansion projects of Peru and Mexico.

SECTION 2 COMPANY DESCRIPTION

2.1 Activities

Southern Copper Corporation, a New York Stock Exchange-listed company, is a leading global producer of copper and other metals, with operations centered in Mexico and Peru. Its core business activities encompass the exploration, mining, smelting, and refining of copper, alongside by-products such as molybdenum, zinc, silver, and gold, which are supplied to industries including construction, electronics, and renewable energy. The company's fastest-growing segments include copper production, fueled by rising demand from electric vehicles and infrastructure development, as well as molybdenum extraction for high-strength alloys in manufacturing. By focusing on operational efficiency and strategic investments in new projects, Southern Copper maintains a competitive edge in the global mining sector, emphasizing sustainable practices to support long-term growth. It is the largest Non ferrous metals sector company by market capitalization among NYSE- and TXSE-listed stocks.

SECTION 2 COMPANY DESCRIPTION

2.1 Activities

Southern Copper Corporation, a New York Stock Exchange-listed company, is a leading global producer of copper and other metals, with operations centered in Mexico and Peru. Its core business activities encompass the exploration, mining, smelting, and refining of copper, alongside by-products such as molybdenum, zinc, silver, and gold, which are supplied to industries including construction, electronics, and renewable energy. The company's fastest-growing segments include copper production, fueled by rising demand from electric vehicles and infrastructure development, as well as molybdenum extraction for high-strength alloys in manufacturing. By focusing on operational efficiency and strategic investments in new projects, Southern Copper maintains a competitive edge in the global mining sector, emphasizing sustainable practices to support long-term growth. It is the largest Non ferrous metals sector company by market capitalization among NYSE- and TXSE-listed stocks.

Southern Copper Corporation (NYSE:SCCO) is a leading integrated copper producer, primarily engaged in open-pit copper mining, smelting, and refining operations across Peru and Mexico. The company operates major mines, including the Toquepala and Cuajone mines, and is advancing projects like the Tia Maria copper project to enhance copper production capacity. Southern Copper's robust ecosystem includes copper concentrate, refined copper, and copper cathode production, supplemented by molybdenum, silver, and sulfuric acid as byproducts. Leveraging extensive copper reserves and efficient mining infrastructure, the company maintains sustainable operations and competitive advantages in the copper expansion projects of Peru and Mexico.

SECTION 2 COMPANY DESCRIPTION

2.1 Activities

Southern Copper Corporation, a New York Stock Exchange-listed company, is a leading global producer of copper and other metals, with operations centered in Mexico and Peru. Its core business activities encompass the exploration, mining, smelting, and refining of copper, alongside by-products such as molybdenum, zinc, silver, and gold, which are supplied to industries including construction, electronics, and renewable energy. The company's fastest-growing segments include copper production, fueled by rising demand from electric vehicles and infrastructure development, as well as molybdenum extraction for high-strength alloys in manufacturing. By focusing on operational efficiency and strategic investments in new projects, Southern Copper maintains a competitive edge in the global mining sector, emphasizing sustainable practices to support long-term growth. It is the largest Non ferrous metals sector company by market capitalization among NYSE- and TXSE-listed stocks.

Incluye detalles de la retransmisión en directo de los resultados

Por Kylie Madry y Natalia Siniawski

CIUDAD DE MÉXICO, 27 oct (Reuters) - La filial de Walmart en México WALMEX.MX no alcanzó el martes las previsiones de beneficios para el tercer trimestre, ya que el aumento de los costos y las inversiones mermaron los márgenes, eclipsando el crecimiento de dos dígitos del comercio electrónico.

El beneficio neto cayó un 6 %, hasta los 11 030 millones de pesos ($610 millones de dólares), por debajo de los 12 260 millones de pesos previstos por los analistas encuestados por LSEG, mientras que los ingresos también se quedaron por debajo de las previsiones.

  • El mayor minorista de México registró unos ingresos totales de 248 830 millones de pesos en el periodo julio-septiembre, un 3 % más que el año anterior, pero por debajo de los 250 440 millones de pesos previstos por los analistas

  • El beneficio antes de intereses, impuestos, depreciaciones y amortizaciones (EBITDA) aumentó solo un 0,4 %, hasta los 25 370 millones de pesos, mientras que el margen EBITDA se redujo en 30 puntos básicos, hasta el 10,2 %

  • La presión sobre los beneficios se debió a que los gastos siguieron aumentando más rápido que las ventas; el director financiero, Camilo Canedo, atribuyó el incremento del gasto a las inversiones en nuevas tiendas, comercio electrónico, tecnología y personal

  • Walmex reafirmó sus previsiones para 2026, pronosticando un crecimiento de las ventas consolidadas de entre el 3,5 % y el 4,5 % en moneda constante y un margen de EBITDA ligeramente inferior al nivel del año pasado, del 10,2 %

  • Las ventas en tiendas comparables aumentaron casi un 2 % en México, donde el valor medio de compra creció un 1,6 % y la afluencia de clientes se mantuvo prácticamente estable

  • El comercio electrónico siguió siendo un punto fuerte, con un valor bruto de la mercancía (GMV) en línea que aumentó un 15 % en México y un 23 % en Centroamérica

  • Canedo señaló que el 75 % de los pedidos en línea se entregaron el mismo día, lo que supone un aumento de 1 500 puntos básicos respecto al año anterior, mientras que casi el 30 % se entregaron en menos de dos horas y cerca del 10 % en menos de una hora

(1 dólar = 18,0808 pesos a finales de septiembre)

• El mayor minorista de México registró unos ingresos totales de 248 830 millones de pesos en el periodo julio-septiembre, un 3 % más que el año anterior, pero por debajo de los 250 440 millones de pesos previstos por los analistas

• El beneficio antes de intereses, impuestos, depreciaciones y amortizaciones (EBITDA) aumentó solo un 0,4 %, hasta los 25 370 millones de pesos, mientras que el margen EBITDA se redujo en 30 puntos básicos, hasta el 10,2 %

• La presión sobre los beneficios se debió a que los gastos siguieron aumentando más rápido que las ventas; el director financiero, Camilo Canedo, atribuyó el incremento del gasto a las inversiones en nuevas tiendas, comercio electrónico, tecnología y personal

• Walmex reafirmó sus previsiones para 2026, pronosticando un crecimiento de las ventas consolidadas de entre el 3,5 % y el 4,5 % en moneda constante y un margen de EBITDA ligeramente inferior al nivel del año pasado, del 10,2 %

• Las ventas en tiendas comparables aumentaron casi un 2 % en México, donde el valor medio de compra creció un 1,6 % y la afluencia de clientes se mantuvo prácticamente estable

• El comercio electrónico siguió siendo un punto fuerte, con un valor bruto de la mercancía (GMV) en línea que aumentó un 15 % en México y un 23 % en Centroamérica

• Canedo señaló que el 75 % de los pedidos en línea se entregaron el mismo día, lo que supone un aumento de 1 500 puntos básicos respecto al año anterior, mientras que casi el 30 % se entregaron en menos de dos horas y cerca del 10 % en menos de una hora

(1 dólar = 18,0808 pesos a finales de septiembre)

SECTION 8 CORPORATE PROFILE

8.1 Activities

Coca-Cola FEMSA, S.A.B. de C.V., is a leading beverage company and the largest franchise bottler for The Coca-Cola Company in Latin America, headquartered in Mexico. Its core business revolves around the production, distribution, and marketing of a diverse portfolio of non-alcoholic beverages, including sparkling drinks, bottled water, juices, teas, and energy drinks, primarily under the Coca-Cola brand. The company operates in key markets such as Mexico, Brazil, Colombia, and Guatemala, utilizing an extensive supply chain and distribution network to reach consumers efficiently. Among its fastest-growing segments are still beverages, particularly flavored waters and ready-to-drink teas, fueled by rising demand for healthier and functional options amid shifting consumer preferences. This growth is supported by strategic investments in innovation, sustainability, and digital platforms, positioning Coca-Cola FEMSA as a resilient player in the competitive beverage industry. It is the International Depository Receipt (IDR) market's 13th largest Beverages company by market capitalization.

SECTION 8 CORPORATE PROFILE

8.1 Activities

Coca-Cola FEMSA, S.A.B. de C.V., is a leading beverage company and the largest franchise bottler for The Coca-Cola Company in Latin America, headquartered in Mexico. Its core business revolves around the production, distribution, and marketing of a diverse portfolio of non-alcoholic beverages, including sparkling drinks, bottled water, juices, teas, and energy drinks, primarily under the Coca-Cola brand. The company operates in key markets such as Mexico, Brazil, Colombia, and Guatemala, utilizing an extensive supply chain and distribution network to reach consumers efficiently. Among its fastest-growing segments are still beverages, particularly flavored waters and ready-to-drink teas, fueled by rising demand for healthier and functional options amid shifting consumer preferences. This growth is supported by strategic investments in innovation, sustainability, and digital platforms, positioning Coca-Cola FEMSA as a resilient player in the competitive beverage industry. It is the International Depository Receipt (IDR) market's 13th largest Beverages company by market capitalization.

SECTION 8 CORPORATE PROFILE

8.1 Activities

Grupo Aeroportuario del Centro Norte S.A.B. de C.V. (OMA), a leading airport operator in Mexico, manages a network of 13 airports primarily in the northern and central regions, including key hubs like Monterrey. Its core business revolves around aeronautical services, such as passenger and cargo handling, alongside non-aeronautical activities including retail concessions, real estate development, and commercial leasing. OMA's fastest-growing segments include international passenger traffic, driven by increasing tourism and trade links, as well as cargo operations, which have expanded with e-commerce and cross-border logistics. Additionally, the company has seen robust growth in non-aeronautical revenues from diversified sources like parking and advertising, supporting overall profitability. Through strategic investments in infrastructure and technology, OMA enhances operational efficiency and passenger experience, positioning itself as a vital player in Mexico's aviation sector. It is the International Depository Receipt (IDR) market's 12th largest Airlines company by market capitalization.

Grupo Aeroportuario del Centro Norte S.A.B. de C.V. (OMA), a leading airport operator in Mexico, manages a network of 13 airports primarily in the northern and central regions, including key hubs like Monterrey. Its core business revolves around aeronautical services, such as passenger and cargo handling, alongside non-aeronautical activities including retail concessions, real estate development, and commercial leasing. OMA's fastest-growing segments include international passenger traffic, driven by increasing tourism and trade links, as well as cargo operations, which have expanded with e-commerce and cross-border logistics. Additionally, the company has seen robust growth in non-aeronautical revenues from diversified sources like parking and advertising, supporting overall profitability. Through strategic investments in infrastructure and technology, OMA enhances operational efficiency and passenger experience, positioning itself as a vital player in Mexico's aviation sector. It is the International Depository Receipt (IDR) market's 12th largest Airlines company by market capitalization.

Promotora y Operadora de Infraestructura, S.A.B. de C.V. (PINFRA), is a leading Mexican company specializing in the development, operation, and maintenance of infrastructure assets. Its core business activities encompass the management of toll road concessions, airport operations, and railway systems, primarily in Mexico, with a focus on enhancing connectivity and efficiency in transportation networks. The company has diversified into complementary areas such as industrial and urban infrastructure projects, leveraging public-private partnerships to drive growth. Among its fastest-growing segments are toll road concessions, fueled by increasing vehicular traffic and strategic expansions, as well as airport operations, which have benefited from rising passenger volumes and modernization efforts. PINFRA's commitment to sustainable practices and operational excellence positions it as a key player in Mexico's infrastructure sector, supporting economic development through reliable and innovative solutions. Finally, HSBC reiterated a "hold" rating and issued a $116.00 price objective (down from $120.00) on shares of Coca Cola Femsa in a research report on Tuesday, July 28th. Four investment analysts have rated the stock with a Buy rating and five have given a Hold rating to the company's stock.   • Positive Sentiment: Consolidated volume increased 5.3% to a record 1.1 billion unit cases, while total revenue rose 10.9% to 79.7 billion Mexican pesos. The results point to continued demand growth across Coca-Cola FEMSAs markets. Coca-Cola FEMSA: 3 Key Takeaways for Long-Term Investors
  • Positive Sentiment: Revenue of approximately $4.41 billion exceeded the consensus estimate of $4.31 billion, indicating that sales momentum was better than analysts expected. Coca-Cola FEMSA Earnings Report

Investors are assessing the companys outlook and whether the strong top-line growth can translate into improved profitability. Coca-Cola FEMSA Q3 2026 Earnings Call Transcript
  • Negative Sentiment: Adjusted earnings per share came in at $1.72, below the $1.89 analyst consensus by $0.17. The shortfall suggests that higher costs, currency effects, or other pressures may have limited the benefit of the companys revenue and volume gains.
  • Negative Sentiment: The earnings miss is likely outweighing the revenue beat in the near term, particularly with the shares trading near their 52-week high. Coca-Cola FEMSA reported an 8.05% net margin, underscoring investor sensitivity to profitability and execution.

Coca Cola Femsa Company Profile

(Free Report)

Coca-Cola FEMSA, SAB. de C.V. is the world's largest Coca-Cola franchise bottler by sales volume. The company produces, markets, sells and distributes beverages under The Coca-Cola Company's brands, including Coca-Cola, Sprite, Fanta and Powerade, as well as bottled water, juices, dairy products, sports drinks, energy drinks and other beverage products.

The company serves consumers through a broad distribution network that includes traditional retail stores, supermarkets, convenience stores, restaurants, food-service businesses and other commercial channels.

SECTION 5 CORPORATE PROFILE

5.1 Activities

Grupo Aeroportuario del Centro Norte S.A.B. de C.V. (OMA), a leading airport operator in Mexico, manages a network of 13 airports primarily in the northern and central regions, including key hubs like Monterrey. Its core business revolves around aeronautical services, such as passenger and cargo handling, alongside non-aeronautical activities including retail concessions, real estate development, and commercial leasing. OMA's fastest-growing segments include international passenger traffic, driven by increasing tourism and trade links, as well as cargo operations, which have expanded with e-commerce and cross-border logistics. Additionally, the company has seen robust growth in non-aeronautical revenues from diversified sources like parking and advertising, supporting overall profitability. Through strategic investments in infrastructure and technology, OMA enhances operational efficiency and passenger experience, positioning itself as a vital player in Mexico's aviation sector. It is the International Depository Receipt (IDR) market's 12th largest Airlines company by market capitalization.

SECTION 5 CORPORATE PROFILE

5.1 Activities

Arca Continental SAB de CV, a prominent Mexican conglomerate, is primarily engaged in the production, bottling, and distribution of beverages as a key franchise partner for The Coca-Cola Company. The company operates across Mexico, the United States, and South America, offering a diverse portfolio that includes carbonated soft drinks, bottled water, juices, teas, and snacks. Its core activities encompass manufacturing, logistics, and sales through an extensive network of distribution channels, serving both retail and hospitality sectors. In recent years, the fastest-growing segments have been healthier beverage options, such as flavored waters and ready-to-drink teas, driven by shifting consumer preferences toward wellness and hydration products. Additionally, international expansion into markets like Ecuador and Peru has fueled growth, enhancing revenue streams and market share. Arca Continental's strategic investments in sustainability and digital technologies further support its operational efficiency and long-term competitiveness in the global beverage industry. It is Mexico's largest Beverages company by market capitalization.

5.1 Activities

Promotora Y Operadora De Infraestructura, S.A.B. De C.V. (PINFRA), a leading Mexican infrastructure company listed on the Mexican Stock Exchange, specializes in the development, construction, operation, and maintenance of transportation and infrastructure assets. Its core activities encompass toll roads, bridges, airports, and railways, primarily through public-private concessions that generate revenue via user fees and long-term contracts. The company plays a vital role in Mexico's economic growth by enhancing connectivity and mobility across key regions. Among its fastest-growing segments are airport operations, which have expanded significantly due to increasing passenger traffic and new terminal developments, as well as concessions for modern toll highways that benefit from rising vehicular demand and government infrastructure initiatives. PINFRA's strategic focus on sustainable projects and operational efficiency has positioned it as a key player in the sector, contributing to national development while delivering consistent returns for shareholders. It is Mexico's 3rd largest Engineering & construction company by market capitalization.

Coca-Cola FEMSA, the leading bottler of the brand by sales volume, has a long-term project to build a new plant in southeastern Mexico, Gerardo Cruz, the company's Chief Financial Officer, announced.

The goal is to reduce transportation costs that have risen due to increased sales volume in the region, he explained during a virtual conference with analysts regarding the results for the third quarter of the year.

Currently, the bottler ships a significant portion of the products made at its plant in Toluca, State of Mexico, to the southeast of the country, which has increased its freight expenses.

"Our freight costs have risen significantly compared to last year," he said. "This is something we are obviously looking to address, taking care of efficiencies in our existing plants in the southeast and with a long-term project for a new plant in that region," he elaborated.

Although the executive did not provide further details regarding the construction of the new plant that they eventually intend to build in southeastern Mexico.

Regarding the performance of the Mexican market, Gerardo Cruz explained that sales volume grew more than expected during the third quarter, driven by demand for larger formats, like the 3-liter Coca-Cola line.

He added that although this boost helped business growth, it also pressured profitability and margins, prompting the company to seek measures to mitigate that effect.

Despite these pressures, including fluctuations in the peso-dollar exchange rate, Pamela Ortiz, the Director of Investor Relations for Coca-Cola FEMSA, highlighted that the company recorded a sequential improvement in profitability compared to the first two quarters, supported by higher volumes and a gradual recovery in operational leverage.

Gaining Market Share in Mexico

In this context, Ian Craig, the Chief Executive Officer of Coca-Cola FEMSA, reported that sales volume in Mexico increased by 4.2% year-on-year during the third quarter, against a low comparison base from the previous year.

He also stated that the bottler gained 70 basis points in value share in carbonated beverages as of September, compared to the same period last year, despite cautious consumer behavior.

The CEO of the bottler emphasized the performance of new products.

During the quarter, the company launched Coca-Cola Triple Zero, as well as Topo Chico Sparkling Lemonade and Orangeade. The latter two beverages achieved 70% coverage in traditional retail and a 40% repurchase rate.

Additionally, Ciel Aguas Frescas, launched in the previous quarter, reached 65% coverage in traditional retail and gained 7.6 percentage points of market share since its launch in May.

Ian Craig stated that Coca-Cola FEMSA continues to perform well commercially, and its innovations are being well received, while remaining alert to potential increases in labor costs, exchange rate movements, and their effect on raw materials.

Therefore, the priority is to maintain volume growth, gain market share, and develop new beverage categories, while gradually improving profitability through disciplined spending of revenues and operational efficiencies.

"We must be aware that the consumption environment remains challenging, but anything we observe now will be practically industry-wide," emphasized the CEO of the bottler.

The period is approaching that requires preparation for the December festivities, and Walmart is aware of this. Therefore, it announced a 14-day discount season for Christmas shopping in 2026 in the United States, featuring three promotional periods that will begin on November 12 and end on December 2. The strategy includes early Black Friday deals , discounts during the traditional Black Friday, and a promotional phase for Cyber Monday .

However, the dates for the U.S. chain should not be confused with the promotional calendar in Mexico . In Mexico, El Buen Fin 2026 will take place from Friday, November 13, to Tuesday, November 17, while Walmart runs its own special promotions and conditions for its stores and nationwide platform.

When will Walmart's Black Friday 2026 be in the United States?

The company confirmed through its official website and social media that there will be three phases of discounts for its U.S. customers. The first will run from November 12 to 15 , with early access for select products available to Walmart+ members. The second phase will span from November 23 to 29 , while Cyber Monday will take place from November 30 to December 2 .

According to Walmart's announcement, online deals will begin at 12:01 AM Eastern Time during both Black Friday events. In physical stores, promotions will start at 6:00 AM local time. For Cyber Monday, the announced start time pertains to the digital platform.

The company has indicated that there will be thousands of gifts available for under $20, and its list of featured toys will include 25 options priced below $25. Additionally, it will offer early access to certain promotions for Walmart+ members, although some deals will be subject to availability and specific conditions.

What will happen with Walmart's offers in Mexico?

In Mexico, the November discount season features El Buen Fin 2026 as one of its central dates, taking place over five days from November 13 to 17 . This initiative brings together registered businesses that offer promotions to encourage shopping and commercial activity.

In previous years, Walmart Mexico has activated a section on its official site dedicated to El Buen Fin offers, categorizing items such as televisions, white goods, computers, groceries, pet supplies, and automotive products. Benefits on its platform include interest-free months on participating products and promotions linked to its payment and delivery services. Conditions depend on the item, payment method, and current promotion.

It is also important to distinguish El Buen Fin from El Fin Irresistible. The former is a national campaign with participation from registered businesses, while the latter is a commercial strategy specific to Walmart in Mexico and Central America. As of the time this article was written, the dates for El Fin Irresistible 2026 have not been officially announced. Therefore, it should not be assumed that it will coincide with the U.S. Black Friday calendar.

Do Walmart's offers in the United States apply in Mexico?

They should not be assumed as valid promotions in both countries. The dates announced by Walmart in the United States pertain solely to that market, and prices, inventories, payment methods, and conditions may vary between national platforms.

Those shopping from Mexico should check directly at Walmart.com.mx and review the conditions of each offer. To consult the registered establishments in El Buen Fin, the official site elbuenfin.org is also available.

Thus, while American shoppers can plan their purchases around the three stages announced by Walmart, the confirmed reference for November in Mexico is El Buen Fin, from the 13th to the 17th. Before making a purchase, it is wise to compare prices, verify interest-free conditions, and confirm that the discount is valid in the country where the transaction will take place.

2.1 Activities

Southern Copper Corporation, a New York Stock Exchange-listed company, is a leading global producer of copper and other metals, with operations centered in Mexico and Peru. Its core business activities encompass the exploration, mining, smelting, and refining of copper, alongside by-products such as molybdenum, zinc, silver, and gold, which are supplied to industries including construction, electronics, and renewable energy. The company's fastest-growing segments include copper production, fueled by rising demand from electric vehicles and infrastructure development, as well as molybdenum extraction for high-strength alloys in manufacturing. By focusing on operational efficiency and strategic investments in new projects, Southern Copper maintains a competitive edge in the global mining sector, emphasizing sustainable practices to support long-term growth. It is the largest Non ferrous metals sector company by market capitalization among NYSE- and TXSE-listed stocks.

SECTION 2 CORPORATE PROFILE

2.1 Activities

Southern Copper Corporation, a New York Stock Exchange-listed company, is a leading global producer of copper and other metals, with operations centered in Mexico and Peru. Its core business activities encompass the exploration, mining, smelting, and refining of copper, alongside by-products such as molybdenum, zinc, silver, and gold, which are supplied to industries including construction, electronics, and renewable energy. The company's fastest-growing segments include copper production, fueled by rising demand from electric vehicles and infrastructure development, as well as molybdenum extraction for high-strength alloys in manufacturing. By focusing on operational efficiency and strategic investments in new projects, Southern Copper maintains a competitive edge in the global mining sector, emphasizing sustainable practices to support long-term growth. It is the largest Non ferrous metals sector company by market capitalization among NYSE- and TXSE-listed stocks.

ADRS AND DEPOSITORY RECEIPTS

America Movil S.A.B. de CV (NYSE:AMX) has jumped 20.3% Year To Date. There is uncertainty in the market and it is difficult to predict how economic conditions will be in 2026 and beyond as well as what the impact of those conditions may be on America Movil S.A.B. de CV. However, there are several key reasons why some investors remain bullish on the long-term prospects for America Movil S.A.B. de CV.

Below are some of those key reasons:

- Return on Assets of 4.9% versus sector average of 2.9% and market average of 1.5%.

- Return on Equity of 20.6% versus sector average of 8.7% and market average of 8.2%.

- Return on Capital Employed of 10.9% versus sector average of 8.5% and market average of 2.9%.

- Total Liabilities/EBITDA of 4.3 is less than 5, this compares favourably with the Joseph Piotroski benchmark of 5.

- As per the Du Pont analysis, Return on Equity is high at 20.6%. This is computed as net profit margin of 9.3% times asset turnover [sales/assets] of 0.52 times leverage factor [total assets/shareholders' equity] of 4.2.Also, this has improved from 6.4% last year.

- Tobin's Q Ratio, defined as MCap divided by Total Assets, is 0.8. Compared with the rest of the market the ADR is undervalued.

However, there are also some reasons investors may remain bearish in the long-term including the following:

- The earnings yield of 0.3% is below the 10-year bond yield of 4.58%.

- The price-to-earnings ratio of 335.3 indicates overvaluation compared with sector average of 19.1 and market average of 15.8.

- Net profit margin has averaged 7.5% in the last 3 years. This is lower than the sector average of 9.3% and suggests a low margin of safety.

Company Profile

Alcaldía Miguel Hidalgo, C.P. 11000, Ciudad de México, México

ORDEN DEL DÍA

ORDEN DEL DÍA

  1. Propuesta, discusión y, en su caso, aprobación de la adquisición por parte del Fideicomiso de un portafolio de activos inmobiliarios integrado por los inmuebles denominados Central Park, Paradox, Lamartine 346 y San Pedro de los Pinos (el "Portafolio Objetivo"), en el entendido de que los inmuebles objeto de adquisición son propiedad de personas relacionadas en términos del Contrato de Fideicomiso y representan 10% (diez por ciento) o más del Patrimonio del Fideicomiso, mediante su aportación al patrimonio del Fideicomiso y la realización de todos los actos, así como la celebración de los contratos y el otorgamiento de las autorizaciones que resulten necesarios o convenientes para su implementación y consumación, para que, en su caso, se faculte al Administrador para determinar los términos y condiciones definitivos de dicha adquisición conforme al Fideicomiso y la Legislación Aplicable. Acciones y resoluciones al respecto.

  2. Propuesta, discusión y, en su caso, aprobación para llevar a cabo una Emisión de CBFIs Adicionales, hasta por la cantidad que determine la Asamblea, que serán mantenidos en la tesorería del Fideicomiso para su eventual utilización conforme a los fines del Fideicomiso, así como de la actualización de la inscripción de los CBFIs en el Registro Nacional de Valores y su listado en la Bolsa Mexicana de Valores, S.A.B. de C.V. Acciones y resoluciones al respecto.

  3. Propuesta, discusión y, en su caso, aprobación de la contratación de créditos bancarios o líneas de crédito con instituciones financieras nacionales o extranjeras conforme a lo establecido en el Contrato de Fideicomiso y los Lineamientos de Apalancamiento previamente aprobados, incluyendo en cada caso la determinación de sus términos y condiciones generales, así como la aprobación de actos, contratos, autorizaciones, delegaciones y demás acciones necesarias o convenientes para llevar a cabo dichas operaciones de financiamiento, en su caso, se faculte al Administrador para determinar los términos y condiciones definitivos de cualquiera de las alternativas antes descritas. Acciones y resoluciones al respecto.

  4. Designación de delegados especiales que, en su caso, formalicen y den cumplimiento a las resoluciones que sean adoptadas en la Asamblea.

REQUISITOS DE ASISTENCIA

Con fundamento en el artículo 221 de la Ley General de Títulos y Operaciones de Crédito, para poder asistir a la Asamblea de Tenedores deberán presentar los pases de asistencia correspondientes a sus CBFIs, expedidos por el Representante Común, por lo que previamente los Tenedores deberán exhibir en las oficinas del Representante Común, ubicadas en Boulevard Manuel Ávila Camacho No. 40, piso 22, Torre Esmeralda 1, Col. Lomas de Chapultepec III Sección, Alcaldía Miguel Hidalgo, C.P. 11000, Ciudad de México, México, a la atención de Alfredo Basurto Dorantes y/o Javier Eduardo Ortega Labastida (alfredo.basurto@multiva.com.mx y/o javiereduardo.ortega@multiva.com.mx, teléfono 555-284-6200 extensiones 54502 y 54503), las respectivas constancias de depósito expedidas por el S.D. Indeval Institución para el Depósito de Valores, S.A. de C.V., complementadas con el listado de Tenedores que para tales efectos formule el custodio correspondiente, en los términos de las disposiciones aplicables de la Ley del Mercado de Valores, dentro del horario

comprendido entre las 9:00 y las 18:00 horas, de lunes a viernes, a partir de la fecha de publicación de la presente convocatoria y hasta cuando menos un día hábil de anticipación a la fecha fijada para la celebración de la Asamblea de Tenedores. Contra entrega de las constancias, se expedirán los respectivos pases de asistencia, en los que constarán el nombre del Tenedor y el número de CBFIs que representen, y sin los cuales no podrán participar en la Asamblea de Tenedores que se convoca.

Los Tenedores podrán ser representados en la Asamblea de Tenedores por apoderados que acrediten su personalidad mediante carta poder o mediante cualquier otra forma de poder otorgado conforme a derecho, que reúnan los requisitos establecidos en el artículo 49 fracción III de la Ley del Mercado de Valores.

La documentación relacionada con cada uno de los puntos del Orden del Día se encontrará a disposición de los Tenedores y del público en general, a partir del día hábil siguiente de la fecha de publicación de la presente Convocatoria, en las oficinas del Representante Común.

ACUERDOS

RESUMEN DE ACUERDOS DE LA ASAMBLEA ORDINARIA DE TENEDORES DE CERTIFICADOS BURSÁTILES FIDUCIARIOS INMOBILIARIOS CON CLAVE DE PIZARRA "FINN 13", EMITIDOS POR BANCO MULTIVA, S.A., INSTITUCIÓN DE BANCA MÚLTIPLE, GRUPO FINANCIERO MULTIVA, DIVISIÓN FIDUCIARIA, ACTUANDO COMO FIDUCIARIA EN EL FIDEICOMISO DB/1616 (ANTERIORMENTE F/1616).

La Asamblea de Tenedores se celebró con un quórum de 627,231,153 Certificados, representando 86.47% del total de Certificados en circulación.

  1. Presentación, discusión y, en su caso, aprobación de la adquisición del inmueble destinado al hospedaje conocido como "Hotel Secrets Puerto Los Cabos Golf & Spa Resort", ubicado en San José del Cabo, Baja California Sur.

    Se hace constar que los Tenedores con conflicto de interés se abstuvieron de deliberar y votar respecto del presente punto del Orden del Día, sin que ello afecte los requisitos de quórum para la instalación de la asamblea, de conformidad con lo establecido en la cláusula Octava, numeral 8.4, inciso (b) del contrato de Fideicomiso Irrevocable identificado con el número DB/1616 (anteriormente F/1616) en el que Banco Multiva, S.A., Institución de Banca Múltiple, Grupo Financiero Multiva es Fiduciario; así mismo, este punto del Orden del Día fue aprobado por

    mayoría de votos de los Tenedores presentes con derecho a votar dicho asunto, de conformidad con las siguientes:

    R E S O L U C I O N E S

    PRIMERA. - Por acuerdo favorable del 98.40% (noventa y ocho punto cuarenta por ciento) de los CBFIs representados en esta Asamblea, se aprueba llevar a cabo la Transacción descrita en el Folleto Informativo y expuesta a esta Asamblea, consistente en la adquisición, directa o indirectamente, por parte del Fideicomiso, del Hotel y de todo lo que de hecho y por derecho le corresponde, sin reserva ni limitación alguna y en el estado en que se encuentre al momento de la Transacción, incluyendo, de manera enunciativa mas no limitativa, bienes inmuebles, construcciones, instalaciones, garantías, bienes intangibles, mobiliario, accesorios, equipamiento, suministros consumibles, inventarios, derechos contractuales, contratos operativos, permisos, licencias, autorizaciones, derechos gubernamentales, derechos de acceso y cualesquiera otros bienes, derechos o activos relacionados con su propiedad, funcionamiento, administración y operación; facultando a los Delegados Especiales de la Transacción (según dicho término se define más adelante) para negociar y determinar los términos definitivos de la Transacción, sin apartarse de los términos generales expuestos en esta Asamblea y sujeto a las facultades que, en su caso, les

    sean otorgadas conforme a la resolución que se adopte al desahogar el segundo punto del Orden del Día de la presente Asamblea.

    SEGUNDA.- Por acuerdo favorable del 98.40% (noventa y ocho punto cuarenta por ciento) de los

    CBFIs representados en esta Asamblea, se aprueba que la contraprestación por la Transacción se calcule sobre un precio de referencia de USD $200,000,000.00 (doscientos millones de dólares 00/100, moneda de curso legal en los Estados Unidos de América), monto que incluye la deuda existente relacionada con el Hotel que sea asumida directa o indirectamente o repagada como parte de la Transacción, de conformidad con lo previsto en la resolución TERCERA siguiente; en el entendido que, para efectos del cálculo de la contraprestación en moneda nacional, se utilizará como referencia el promedio del tipo de cambio peso-dólar publicado por el Banco de México durante los 20 (veinte) días hábiles previos a la fecha en que se consume la Transacción, conforme se establezca en los documentos definitivos de la Transacción.

    TERCERA.- Por acuerdo favorable del 98.40% (noventa y ocho punto cuarenta por ciento) de los CBFIs representados en esta Asamblea, se aprueba que la contraprestación por la Transacción sea pagadera mediante: (i) la asunción directa o indirecta o el repago de la deuda existente relacionada con el Hotel, según se determine conforme a la estructura final de la Transacción y sujeto a las autorizaciones, consentimientos y dispensas que resulten aplicables; y (ii) la entrega del número de CBFIs que corresponda por el remanente de la contraprestación, una vez deducido el monto correspondiente al fondeo del repago o la asunción de la deuda señalada en el inciso anterior, considerando para dichos efectos un precio de $5.40 M.N. (cinco pesos 40/100, Moneda Nacional) por cada CBFI. Asimismo, se aprueba que el Impuesto al Valor Agregado y demás impuestos que, en su caso, sean a cargo del Fideicomiso conforme a la legislación aplicable, sean pagados en efectivo.

    CUARTA.- Por acuerdo favorable del 98.40% (noventa y ocho punto cuarenta por ciento) de los CBFIs representados en esta Asamblea, se autoriza que la Transacción pueda estructurarse y ejecutarse mediante una o varias operaciones, simultáneas o sucesivas, incluyendo, sin limitar, la aportación del Hotel al patrimonio del Fideicomiso, la adquisición de la totalidad de los derechos fideicomisarios del fideicomiso que detente la propiedad del Hotel, la compraventa de activos, la transmisión de activos, derechos, permisos, licencias, contratos y demás elementos necesarios para su operación, o cualquier otra estructura legal, fiscal, financiera, corporativa u operativa que resulte conveniente para el Fideicomiso; facultando a los Delegados Especiales de la Transacción para negociar y determinar los términos definitivos de la Transacción, sin apartarse de los términos generales expuestos en esta Asamblea y sujeto a las facultades que, en su caso, les sean otorgadas conforme a la resolución que se adopte al desahogar el segundo punto del Orden del Día de la presente Asamblea.

    QUINTA. - Por acuerdo favorable del 98.40% (noventa y ocho punto cuarenta por ciento) de los CBFIs representados en esta Asamblea, se autoriza e instruye al Fiduciario para que, según lo determinen los Delegados Especiales de la Transacción: (i) fondee el repago de la deuda existente relacionada con el Hotel frente a BBVA México, S.A., Institución de Banca Múltiple, Grupo Financiero BBVA México o quien corresponda; o (ii) asuma, directa o indirectamente, dicha deuda, así como cualesquier obligaciones relacionadas o accesorias, incluyendo, sin limitar, las garantías otorgadas al amparo de dicha deuda.

    SEXTA. - Por acuerdo favorable del 98.40% (noventa y ocho punto cuarenta por ciento) de los CBFIs representados en esta Asamblea, se autoriza al Fiduciario para que lleve a cabo cualquier trámite o gestión, celebre, suscriba y/o comparezca a la celebración de toda clase de documentos,

    convenios, contratos, certificaciones, así como para realizar toda clase de pagos, depósitos, asientos, notificaciones, avisos, transferencias y demás actividades y actos necesarios o convenientes para formalizar los actos autorizados en la resolución inmediata anterior, incluyendo, sin limitar, la suscripción de cualquier título de crédito. Para lo anterior, se faculta a los Delegados Especiales de

    la Transacción para determinar los términos y condiciones para la celebración de cualesquiera de los actos o documentos antes referidos.

    SÉPTIMA. - Por acuerdo favorable del 98.40% (noventa y ocho punto cuarenta por ciento) de los CBFIs representados en esta Asamblea, se autoriza e instruye al Fiduciario para que lleve a cabo cualesquiera actos, trámites, gestiones, avisos, solicitudes, comparecencias, notificaciones, promociones, escritos, manifestaciones, aclaraciones, requerimientos, respuestas, pagos de derechos, autorizaciones, registros, inscripciones y demás actuaciones que resulten necesarias o

    convenientes ante cualquier autoridad, organismo, entidad gubernamental, órgano constitucional

    autónomo, dependencia, comisión, registro público, fedatario público o tercero, ya sea federal, estatal o municipal, en México o en el extranjero, en relación con la Transacción, incluyendo, sin limitar, la presentación, seguimiento y desahogo de la notificación de concentración que, en su caso, deba realizarse ante la Comisión Nacional Antimonopolio, así como la obtención de cualesquiera autorizaciones, aprobaciones, consentimientos, dispensas, resoluciones, constancias, opiniones, registros o confirmaciones que resulten necesarias o convenientes para implementar, perfeccionar y consumar la Transacción conforme a lo aprobado por esta Asamblea.

  2. Propuesta, discusión y, en su caso, aprobación para otorgar facultades a los Delegados Especiales en relación con la implementación, perfeccionamiento y consumación de la adquisición.

    Se hace constar que los Tenedores con conflicto de interés se abstuvieron de deliberar y votar respecto del presente punto del Orden del Día, sin que ello afecte los requisitos de quórum para la instalación de la asamblea, de conformidad con lo establecido en la cláusula Octava, numeral 8.4, inciso (b) del contrato de Fideicomiso Irrevocable identificado con el número DB/1616 (anteriormente F/1616) en el que Banco Multiva, S.A., Institución de Banca Múltiple, Grupo Financiero Multiva es Fiduciario; así mismo, este punto del Orden del Día fue aprobado por

    mayoría de votos de los Tenedores presentes con derecho a votar dicho asunto, de conformidad con las siguientes:

    R E S O L U C I O N E S

    OCTAVA.- Por acuerdo favorable del 98.40% (noventa y ocho punto cuarenta por ciento) de los CBFIs representados en esta Asamblea, se autoriza instruir y delegar plenas facultades a los Delegados Especiales de la Transacción para que, conjunta o separadamente, negocien e instruyan al Fiduciario para otorgar, celebrar, suscribir, modificar, ratificar y/o terminar cualesquiera

    acuerdos, convenios, contratos, instrumentos y/o documentos, así como para realizar cualquier acto que sea necesario y/o conveniente para implementar, perfeccionar y consumar la Transacción y los demás actos a que se refieren las resoluciones del primer punto del Orden del Día.

    NOVENA.- Por acuerdo favorable del 98.40% (noventa y ocho punto cuarenta por ciento) de los CBFIs representados en esta Asamblea, se designa a los señores Jaime Cohen Bistre, Héctor Rodrigo Vázquez Montoya y Lizeth Mariel Pedraza Nava como Delegados Especiales de la transacción (los "Delegados Especiales de la Transacción"), para que conjunta o separadamente, puedan negociar y, en su caso, rechazar los términos y condiciones de la Transacción con sus contrapartes, así como instruir al Fiduciario para llevar a cabo todos los actos que sean necesarios y/o convenientes para consumar dicha Transacción. Para tales efectos, los Delegados Especiales de la Transacción podrán realizar, de manera enunciativa mas no limitativa, lo siguiente: (i) negociar e instruir al Fiduciario para que suscriba, modifique, ratifique y/o termine cualquier mandato,

    acuerdo, convenio, contrato, instrumento, documento y/o información que estimen necesaria y/o conveniente con relación a, o para implementar, perfeccionar y/o consumar, la Transacción; (ii) instruir al Fiduciario para que presente cualquier tipo de solicitudes, lleve a cabo todos los trámites

    así como celebrar, suscribir y/o comparecer a la celebración de toda clase de documentos, convenios, contratos, certificaciones, escrituras, instrumentos e instrucciones; (iv) determinar los términos y condiciones del acto, contrato, convenio o instrumento de que se trate, incluyendo, sin limitar, declaraciones, obligaciones de hacer y no hacer, condiciones suspensivas, cláusulas de indemnización y contribución, limitaciones de responsabilidad, garantías, mecanismos de cierre,

    el Notario Público de su elección con el fin de protocolizar total o parcialmente el presente documento y, en su caso, inscriba el testimonio respectivo en el Registro Público de Comercio correspondiente.

  5. Redacción, lectura y, en su caso, aprobación del Acta de Asamblea.

R E S O L U C I Ó N

DÉCIMA TERCERA.- Se aprueba el acta levantada con motivo de la presente Asamblea Ordinaria de Tenedores y se instruye al Fiduciario la realización de los actos aquí referidos,

tomando la presente acta como carta de instrucción para todos los efectos legales a que haya lugar.

Oct 25, 2026

Coca Cola Femsa (NYSE:KOF) reported record third-quarter volume, with consolidated unit case volume rising 5.3% year over year to 1.1 billion. Revenue increased 10.9% to MXN 79.7 billion, while majority net income rose 5.5% to MXN 6.2 billion.

CEO Ian Craig said the companys results reflected commercial strategies tailored to different consumer and macroeconomic conditions across its markets. He cited the companys brand portfolio, distribution network, investments in marketing, customer execution and digital tools as key competitive advantages.

The company also discussed relief efforts following an August earthquake in Colombia that affected Pereira and Cali. Craig said Coca-Cola FEMSA, FEMSA and The Coca-Cola Company provided more than 180,000 liters of water, 30,000 meals and other supplies, while committing support for more than 1,000 traditional trade stores and the rebuilding of about 150 stores.

Profitability Supported by Lower Input Costs

Gross profit increased 14.5% to MXN 37 billion, and gross margin expanded 140 basis points to 46.5%. CFO Gerardo Cruz said lower sweetener and PET costs, supported by commodity hedging and appreciation in most operating currencies against the U.S. dollar, helped offset higher aluminum costs and unfavorable mix effects.

Operating income rose 15.4% to MXN 11.9 billion, with operating margin increasing 60 basis points to 14.9%. However, reported operating income included MXN 1.1 billion of recovered insurance claims in Brazil. Excluding that non-recurring recovery, operating income would have risen 7.4% and operating margin would have been 13.6%, a 40-basis-point contraction.

Adjusted EBITDA rose 16.2% to MXN 16.8 billion, producing a 21.1% margin. Excluding the Brazilian insurance recovery, adjusted EBITDA increased 10.6%, with a 19.7% margin.

Net financing expense increased to MXN 2 billion from MXN 1.3 billion a year earlier. Cruz attributed the increase primarily to higher interest expenses following debt issuance in the first quarter, as well as a MXN 377 million loss on financial instruments, compared with a MXN 39 million loss a year earlier, largely reflecting higher interest rates in Brazil.

Mexico Volumes Recover, but Costs Pressure Margins

Mexico volume increased 4.2% year over year, aided by affordability initiatives, price-pack architecture and commercial execution. Craig said the comparison reflected a low base in the prior year, when consumer backlash had affected results. The company reported a 70-basis-point increase in sparkling beverage value share in Mexico as of September.

The company introduced Coca-Cola Triple Zero, Topo Chico Sparkling Lemonade and Orangeade, and Ciel Aguas Frescas. Topo Chicos new sparkling products reached 70% coverage in traditional trade and recorded a 40% repurchase rate, according to Craig. Ciel Aguas Frescas reached 65% traditional-trade coverage and gained 7.6 percentage points of market share since its May launch.

Mexico and Central America volume rose 4.8%, while revenue grew 8.3% to MXN 46 billion. Operating income in the region declined 3.1% to MXN 6.5 billion and margin contracted 170 basis points to 14.3%, though management said profitability improved sequentially from the first two quarters.

Management pointed to a higher mix of multi-serve products, particularly 3-liter Coca-Cola packages, as a source of price-mix and margin pressure. It also cited marketing, labor and freight expenses, along with an operating foreign-exchange loss. Freight costs increased as the company shipped product from its Toluca plant to southeastern Mexico, with management pursuing plant efficiencies and a longer-term new plant project in the region.

Craig said pricing and revenue growth management initiatives introduced in August were well received, and the company expects to take additional actions as needed to address foreign-exchange, labor and raw-material pressures.

South America Delivers Growth Across Markets

South America volume increased 6% to 448 million unit cases, while revenue rose 14.7% to MXN 33.7 billion. Operating income increased 51.2% to MXN 5.3 billion, including the Brazilian insurance recovery. Cruz said underlying profitability also benefited from operating leverage, favorable mix and expense efficiencies.

Brazil volume increased 3.9%. Coca-Cola Zero volume grew 15%, while flavors and still beverages increased 8% and 20%, respectively. The company said it gained approximately 1.2 percentage points of share in total nonalcoholic ready-to-drink beverages and nearly 6 percentage points in energy drinks.

Craig said management remains mindful of a possible post-election slowdown in Brazil, as well as potential selective-tax and labor-reform effects. If such measures create non-neutral costs, the company intends to use revenue growth management initiatives and productivity actions to address them.

Colombia volume increased 15.9%, supported by consumer demand, household purchasing power, weather conditions and GDP growth of approximately 3.5%, according to management. Sparkling beverage volume rose 15.4%, while year-to-date non-carbonated beverage volume grew 12.9%. The company said its Fury launch reached 30% customer coverage in its first month.

Craig said demand in Colombia and Venezuela has outpaced expectations, creating capacity constraints and low inventory levels. The company is investing in those markets but described the supply environment as tight.

Guatemala volume grew 8%, above an estimated 5.5% expansion in the local nonalcoholic ready-to-drink industry. Energy drink volume rose 98%, while the company reported a roughly 1-percentage-point gain in sports-drink market share. Argentina volume was flat amid pressure on household purchasing power, though sparkling beverages grew 3.9%.

Digital Tools and Hedging Remain Strategic Priorities

Management said its Juntos+ digital platform continues to support customer engagement and larger order values. In Mexico, Juntos+ drove a 19% increase in average ticket, while digital revenue in Brazil represented nearly 42% of traditional-trade revenue and average ticket increased 18%.

The company plans to expand its Juntos+ Advisor salesforce tool, including order-entry capabilities in Mexico and additional deployment across Latin America. Craig said a new supervisor tool being piloted in Brazil is designed to provide real-time visibility into salesforce gaps and coaching opportunities.

For 2026, Coca-Cola FEMSA said it had hedged about 65% of PET requirements, 88% of sugar, 98% of high-fructose corn syrup and 74% of aluminum. For 2027, it had secured approximately 16% of PET, 85% of sugar, 94% of high-fructose corn syrup and 54% of aluminum requirements, at prices broadly in line with 2026 levels for the portion secured.

Cruz also said the company expects to announce a shareholder capital-return mechanism early next year after completing its analysis of balance-sheet and capital-allocation options.

About Coca Cola Femsa (NYSE:KOF)

Coca-Cola FEMSA, SAB. de C.V. is the world's largest Coca-Cola franchise bottler by sales volume. The company produces, markets, sells and distributes beverages under The Coca-Cola Company's brands, including Coca-Cola, Sprite, Fanta and Powerade, as well as bottled water, juices, dairy products, sports drinks, energy drinks and other beverage products.

The company serves consumers through a broad distribution network that includes traditional retail stores, supermarkets, convenience stores, restaurants, food-service businesses and other commercial channels.

Nov 18, 2025: ASUR SIGNS DEAL TO ACQUIRE MOTIVA'S STAKE IN AIRPORT BUSINESS IN BRAZIL, ECUADOR, COSTA RICA AND CURACAO

Grupo Aeroportuario del Sureste, S.A.B. de C.V. (NYSE:ASR; BMV:ASUR) ("ASUR") and Motiva Infraestrutura de Mobilidade S.A. (B3: MOTV3) ("Motiva") today announced that ASUR has entered into a purchase agreement with Motiva to acquire all of the issued and outstanding equity interest of Companhia de Participacoes em Concessoes ("CPC"), a wholly owned subsidiary of Motiva, for a purchase price of R$5,000 million (US$936 million)1,2, with an implied enterprise value R$13,700 million (US$2,566 million) 2,3. CPC owns equity interests in 20 airports with concessions in Brazil, Ecuador, Costa Rica and Curacao. The portfolio includes the Quito International Airport in Quito, Ecuador, the Juan Santamaria International Airport in San Jose, Costa Rica, the Curacao International Airport in Curacao, the Confins International Airport in Brazil, as well as the Pampulha airport, the Bloco Sul airports, and the Bloco Central airports in Brazil. The portfolio reported EBITDA for the twelve- month period ending September 30, 2025, on an 100% basis, of R$2,000 million (US$375 million 2 ) and, on a proportionate basis to CPC's stake, of R$1,300 million (US$243 million 2 ); and, net financial debt as of September 30, 2025, on an 100% basis, of R$6,300 million (US$1,180 million 2 ). The acquisition represents a stepping stone in ASUR's expansion strategy in the region adding 4 new markets in Latin America and the Caribbean, including Latin America's largest aviation market by passengers, Brazil, to ASUR's existing presence in Mexico, Colombia and Puerto Rico. This acquisition will add more than 45 million passengers to ASUR's 71 million reported in 2024, consolidating ASUR as the leading airport operator in the Americas. Out of the 20 airports in CPC's portfolio, 17 have more than 15 years remaining in their concession life.
